concept: Interaction-picture simulation separates dominant and interaction Hamiltonian components
summary: For Hamiltonians that can be written as a dominant component plus an interaction component, the interaction picture can transform the problem into time-dependent evolution where complexity depends more favorably on the interaction component when the dominant part is cheaply evolvable.
applies_to: Hamiltonians with a dominant exactly or cheaply simulable component
limitations: Requires a meaningful split of the Hamiltonian into dominant and interaction components.
Requires an implementation contract beyond the current simple terms/t interface.
Uses time-dependent simulation machinery, so implementation complexity is higher than direct product formulas.
implications: Do not implement interaction-picture evolution until OpenQEvo defines a split-Hamiltonian input contract.
Consider this family when direct Trotterization is too expensive because of a large but cheaply evolvable dominant component.
Treat interaction-picture recommendations as non-executable until method metadata and software registration exist.

evidence.note: Develops Hamiltonian simulation in the interaction picture and analyzes favorable complexity tradeoffs for split Hamiltonians.
Existing trotterization source covering hybridized interaction-picture simulation methods.
